name: Peppermint Oil
summary: Peppermint Oil carries a Grade D rating — preliminary / theoretical evidence. Strongest recorded design is a meta-analysis, drawn from 4 recorded studies, 4 in people. No disagreement is recorded across them. Recorded activity centres on antispasmodic effect on GI smooth muscle., which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Noted cautions include hiatal hernia due to worsened reflux symptoms.
description: Peppermint oil can relax gastrointestinal smooth muscle and reduce visceral pain signaling, aligning with evidence for IBS symptom reduction and abdominal discomfort.
safetyNotes: Can worsen reflux; use enteric-coated products for IBS contexts.

qualifiers.dose_or_duration: enteric-coated delayed-release peppermint oil TID; 8 weeks

sources.title: The effect of enteric-coated, delayed-release peppermint oil on irritable bowel syndrome
sources.citation: PubMed PMID 19507027. Minimal citation row added from existing workbook PMID; title/year/journal still require PubMed metadata extraction.

contraindications: gastroesophageal reflux disease or active gastric ulcers due to decreased lower esophageal sphincter pressure worsening reflux
gallstones or bile duct obstruction or gallbladder inflammation or severe liver damage
cyclosporine due to slowed drug breakdown and increased blood levels
acid-reducing medications such as antacids or proton pump inhibitors or H2 blockers may cause enteric-coated capsules to dissolve prematurely in the stomach
hiatal hernia due to worsened reflux symptoms
